acts.20.p1.b1.text: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

acts.20.p1.b2.text: And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.

acts.20.p1.b3.text: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.

acts.20.p1.b4.text: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.

acts.20.p2.b5.text: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.

acts.20.p2.b6.text: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

acts.20.p2.b7.text: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep

acts.20.p3.b8.text: as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story

acts.20.p3.b10.text: “Do not be alarmed! … He is still alive!”

acts.20.p4.b11.text: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak,

acts.20.p4.b13.text: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.

acts.20.p5.b14.text: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.

acts.20.p5.b15.text: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard

acts.20.p5.b16.text: … he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

acts.20.p6.b17.text: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

acts.20.p6.b18.text: “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia. I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, …”

acts.20.p6.b19.text: “… I taught you publicly and from house to house …”

acts.20.p7.b20.text: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.

acts.20.p7.b21.text: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.

acts.20.p7.b22.text: “But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course …”

acts.20.p7.b23.text: “… and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.”

acts.20.p8.b24.text: “Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.”

acts.20.p8.b25.text: “Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock … Be shepherds of the church of God …”

acts.20.p8.b26.text: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.

acts.20.p8.b27.text: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.

acts.20.p9.b28.text: “And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace …”

acts.20.p9.b29.text: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

acts.20.p9.b30.text: “… remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

acts.20.p10.b31.text: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

acts.20.p10.b32.text: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

acts.20.p10.b33.text: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again.

acts.20.p10.b34.text: Then they accompanied him to the ship.
